DIAGNOSIS READY: Incus Dislocation (Secondary to Cholesteatoma/Recurrent Otitis Media Post-Tympanoplasty).

The tenderness near the tonsillar area, combined with pain triggered by chewing and earring pressure after tympanoplasty, strongly suggests a structural problem in the middle ear, such as a dislocated incus or a cholesteatoma eroding into the ossicles. The normal initial exams make external causes unlikely, pointing toward an internal mechanical defect or recurrent disease.

REQUEST TEST: High-resolution CT of the temporal bone (if not already reviewed for ossicular chain integrity).
